page: UpCloud HIMEM-4xCPU-32GB is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 4 shared vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 100 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results indicate a clear tradeoff between memory capacity and processing performance. The shared AMD EPYC CPU delivers weak to poor compute performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 10% and multi-core in the bottom 25%. Geekbench multi-core and software compilation tests also fall into the bottom 25%. However, memory bandwidth read-only tests for both small cached blocks (415.18 GB/sec) and large uncached blocks (41.36 GB/sec) perform in the middle 50%, though write bandwidth for large blocks is weaker at 19.09 GB/sec. Passmark CPU scores and single-threaded decompression benchmarks remain in the average tier.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance compute resources. The shared CPU allocation and weak database operations (1901.13 in Passmark) and Redis SET performance (5.28 million operations per second) suggest it is less suited for high-throughput transactional databases. Instead, it is appropriate for memory-intensive applications with moderate CPU demands, such as caching layers, lightweight data processing, and small-scale LLM inference using models under 7B parameters.
